title: Jump Left or Right to Reach a Zero

concept.title: An array with jump rules is a graph: positions are nodes and jumps are edges
body: You stand on position `s` of an array. From position `i` you may jump to `i + arr[i]` or to `i - arr[i]`, as long as the new position is inside the array. Can you reach a position that holds a 0? The graph is **hidden in the rules**: the nodes are the positions `1..n`, and every position has at most two outgoing edges, to `i + arr[i]` and `i - arr[i]`. No edge list is needed, because the neighbours of a position are computed from its value.

So it is reachability again: a search from `s` that follows jumps and stops when it finds a 0. Mark the positions as seen so that no position is processed twice (the jumps can go back and forth, so without marks the search could run for ever).
There are `n` nodes and at most `2n` edges, so the search takes O(n) time. Recognising that a puzzle is a graph is half of the work in many problems.

statement: An array has `n` non-negative numbers. You start at position `s` (positions are numbered from 1). From position `i` you can jump to position `i + arr[i]` or to position `i - arr[i]` (only if the position exists). Print `yes` if you can reach a position whose value is 0, and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `s`: the length of the array and the starting position (counted from 1).
The second line has the `n` numbers of the array.

examples.note: From position 6 (value 1) jump to 5 (value 3), then to 2 (value 2), then to 4, where the value is 0: yes.

hints: The positions are the nodes; from i the neighbours are i + arr[i] and i - arr[i].
Run a search from s and mark positions as seen.
Stop with yes as soon as you reach a position with the value 0.

explanation: The positions are nodes with at most two jumps each; a search from the start position marks the reachable positions and stops with yes at a position with value 0.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, s = map(int, input().split())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = [False] * (n + 1)
seen[s] = True
stack = [s]
found = False
while stack:
    i = stack.pop()
    if arr[i - 1] == 0:
        found = True
        break
    for j in (i + arr[i - 1], i - arr[i - 1]):
        if 1 <= j <= n and not seen[j]:
            seen[j] = True
            stack.append(j)
print("yes" if found else "no")
